records.reported_operational_impact: BusinessMirror reported that more than 1,000 workers struck after bargaining talks reached a deadlock, halting production for 74 hours. The strike ended on 8 March after a settlement confirmed by the labor secretary.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed factual summary and link only.

limitations: IndustriALL's account at https://www.industriall-union.org/union-win-at-nexperia-philippines-inc-after-three-day-strike says the strike began on 6 March, conflicting with BusinessMirror's 5 March date. The earlier reported date is retained for retrieval; the discrepancy is unresolved.
The 8 March date is the reported end of the strike, not verified restoration of normal output, order delivery, or supply-chain recovery.
The reported duration and production stoppage come from the news report and are not independently measured against factory output records.
Electronic components provide context for the supplied electrical product categories; no case-study part, supplier relationship, or shipment has been verified.
MATERIAL-2025-CN-CHIP-001 concerns a different Nexperia supply disruption in China in October 2025, not this strike.

search_window.note: The reported strike dates and seven additional days after its reported end are included for retrieval only; the buffer is not an observed recovery period.

records.reported_operational_impact: Carscoops reported that approximately 1,000 UAW workers walked out at a plant producing axles for GM pickup trucks. WMUK reported that members ratified a contract on 14 June, ending the strike.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed factual summary and links only.

limitations: Start date, approximate worker count and axle application are reported by https://www.carscoops.com/2026/06/american-axle-uaw-strike/; WMUK independently describes the strike and ratification.
The strike end is the reported ratification date; normal plant output, fulfillment of backlogs, and shipment recovery dates are not established.
Potential interruption to GM production was reported as a risk, not an observed shutdown; no downstream shutdown is asserted.
Vehicle parts appear in the supplied descriptions, but no case-study component, buyer, or shipment is linked to the plant.

search_window.note: The reported strike dates plus seven days after reported ratification are included for retrieval only; the buffer is not a measured recovery period.

records.reported_operational_impact: The Teamsters reported on 24 March that 60 Local 3 members had launched a strike after their contract expired. Industry reporting identifies the site as a corrugated packaging plant and says other unions at the facility were not participating.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and source links only.

limitations: The strike's exact start and end dates, duration, production volume lost, and order delays were not established; contract expiry on 23 March is not a verified strike start.

Industry account https://www.paperadvance.com/news/industry-news/strike-at-smurfit-westrock-plant-ahead-of-closure.html reports a separately planned closure and other nonparticipating unions. The closure is not asserted to have resulted from the strike.
The union describes its action as an unfair labor practice strike; the employer disputed its characterization and reported good-faith negotiations in the industry account.
Corrugated packaging is in the supplied list, but the report identifies food-service packaging and no case-study buyer or shipment.

search_window.note: Fourteen days either side of the union's 24 March report for retrieval only; the buffer is not a verified strike or recovery interval.

records.disruption_type: warehouse labour action; operational impact disputed
records.reported_operational_impact: City News Service reported a union-organized action on 2 September. The Teamsters claimed a 24-hour work stoppage involving both primary shifts; Amazon denied operational disruption and disputed that employees participated.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and link only.

limitations: The union and company disagree about worker participation, representation, and whether the facility stopped. Neither version of the operational impact was independently established.
The 24-hour stoppage is a union claim, not a verified event duration; the end date and any backlog or recovery are unknown.
Reported allegations about the parties' conduct are disputed claims, not independently established findings.
A general warehouse labour action offers logistics context only; no case-study product, supplier, route, or shipment is identified.

search_window.note: The reported action date and a 14-day retrieval-only buffer do not establish an operational stoppage, incident end, or recovery duration.
